title: Killing a Cat Was a Capital Crime
hook: In ancient Egypt, if your house caught fire, saving the family cat came before saving your own furniture.

scenes.text: Ancient Egyptians revered cats not merely as beloved household pets, but as sacred earthly protectors linked to the goddess Bastet.

scenes.text: Cats guarded granaries against mice and killed venomous horned vipers, safeguarding the entire family's survival and food supply.

scenes.text: Egyptian law was merciless: killing a cat, even completely by accident, carried an automatic mandatory death sentence by mob stoning.

scenes.text: Historian Herodotus wrote that during a house fire, Egyptians formed human cordons to save cats before extinguishing the flames.
